claims.text: The owner proposes explorer coding as a better name for what is usually called vibe coding.
claims.quote: I would like to propose a better name for what is usually called vibe coding: explorer coding.

claims.text: The term vibe coding is Andrej Karpathy's, from a post in February 2025 about throwaway weekend projects, and by November it was Collins Dictionary's word of the year.
claims.quote: He was describing throwaway weekend projects, and by November it was Collins Dictionary's word of the year.

claims.text: Andrew Ng said in May 2025 that it is unfortunate the practice is called vibe coding, and that coding with AI is a deeply intellectual exercise.
claims.quote: It's unfortunate that that's called vibe coding

claims.text: Explorer is Simon Wardley's word for people who explore the uncharted land, who show you wonder but fail a lot, which is what someone building their own tool with an agent does.
claims.quote: They show you wonder but they fail a lot.

claims.text: The owner could not find anyone using explorer coding as a term; the nearest is exploratory programming, the research term for programming while requirements are still being discovered.
claims.quote: I could not find anyone using explorer coding as a term.

claims.text: Spreadsheets won because of the feedback loop, change a cell and see the result, and what has changed is that the loop is now fast for anything.
claims.quote: Spreadsheets won because of the feedback loop

claims.text: The owner thinks this is the best thing to happen to software since the spreadsheet, an explosion of empowerment.
claims.quote: That is why I think it is the best thing to happen to software since the spreadsheet

claims.text: When someone in HR explored what her team would build and the agents they would manage, her answer was Amazing! When can I start?
claims.quote: her answer was: "Amazing! When can I start?"

claims.text: What explorers produce is the best brief there is: a working app says what its user wants better than any document, because it runs.
claims.quote: A working app says what its user wants better than any document, because it runs.

claims.text: An explorer-coded app may look and feel like an application, but nobody has read the code or validated the architecture, and it is not ready to be in line.
claims.quote: Nobody has read the code. Nobody has validated the architecture.

claims.text: Dependence comes quickly: once something gets used it is mission critical, even for one person, and from then on it has to be maintained and kept working.
claims.quote: Once something gets used, it is mission critical, because people depend on it

claims.text: Villagers take what the explorer built and make it safe to depend on: maintenance, tests, releases that do not break it, agent behaviour policies and rules for the data the agents touch.
claims.quote: That is the villagers' work.

claims.text: The Linux kernel's rules say AI agents must not add Signed-off-by tags, only humans can certify the Developer Certificate of Origin, and the submitter takes full responsibility.
claims.quote: AI agents MUST NOT add Signed-off-by tags

claims.text: Fedora's policy proposal says the contributor is always the author and fully accountable for their contributions.
claims.quote: The contributor is always the author and is fully accountable for their contributions.

claims.text: An explorer cannot be made accountable for code they never read; the team the work is handed to can, and the town planners above all.
claims.quote: We cannot make an explorer accountable for code they never read.

claims.text: The further towards commodity the code sits on the map, the fewer agents in line and the more deterministic code, as argued for code review and for cost.
claims.quote: the further towards commodity, the fewer agents in line, and the more deterministic code

claims.text: Every product needs an explorer version, in which users talk to the product with a model, reshape it and keep their own version, with paid conversions to a villager product and a town planner one.
claims.quote: Products need to become explorer-friendly; more than that, they need an explorer version.

claims.text: Each conversion step is a revenue stream, and each submission tells the vendor exactly what its users want.
claims.quote: Each step is a revenue stream, and each submission tells the vendor exactly what its users want.

claims.text: The same path should exist inside companies and around open-source projects; the custom Firefox plan walks through it for one product.
claims.quote: The custom Firefox plan walks through what it would look like for one product.

claims.text: Explorer coding is a proposal; the owner found no established use of the term, and exploratory programming is its ancestor.
claims.quote: Explorer coding is a proposal.

claims.text: The article does not claim explorer-coded apps are good code; the point is that they are briefs, not products.
claims.quote: Not that explorer-coded apps are good code.

claims.text: The HR conversation is one conversation, an illustration and not a survey.
claims.quote: The HR conversation is one conversation.

claims.text: The explorer version of a product is a proposal; the owner knows of no vendor selling it.
claims.quote: The explorer version of a product is a proposal.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 16 October 2026, written by the site's agent in the site's voice, with the sources read the same day.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 16 October 2026, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site

claims.text: In September the owner wrote that the word vibe coding had won; now he goes further, because the word is doing harm and is a little demeaning to the people doing it.
claims.quote: I want to go further now, because the word is doing harm.
